text:
customer.ops: Hey team, prod-service target group is showing 0/3 healthy on the NLB and we're getting intermittent 502s from the API. Customer says it started ~20m ago after a deploy. NLB health check status says 'TLS handshake failure'. Can someone help triage?

maria-support: Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the target group health-check config + a snippet of Envoy logs? Also which target type (ip/instance)?

customer.ops: target type = ip, targets on private subnets. Health check config: protocol=HTTPS, port=443, path=/health, interval=10s, timeout=5s, healthy threshold=3, Host = (blank). Envoy logs show repeated: "TLS handshake failed: unsupported SNI='10.0.3.12'" and then connection closed.

lee-network: Hmm if Host is blank, AWS health checks will send SNI based on the IP by default in some setups. If Envoy expects SNI 'prod-service.internal' it'll drop a handshake for '10.0.x.x'. Can you reproduce locally from a jump host?

customer.ops: Ran this from the bastion:
```
# without SNI
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.3.12:443 < /dev/null 2>&1 | head -n 20
```
Response shows cert for prod-service.internal but server immediately closed with: "TLS alert number 40".

alice-oncall: Try with explicit SNI:
```
openssl s_client -connect 10.0.3.12:443 -servername prod-service.internal
```
If that succeeds but the plain connect fails, SNI mismatch is almost certainly the cause.

customer.ops: confirmed: with -servername it returns full cert chain and HTTP 200 on /health (we did curl --resolve to test). Without -servername the handshake bails.

jake-devops: Root cause explanation — NLB HTTP(S) health checks will perform TLS handshake and will set the SNI to the Host header if configured. If Host is blank, some LB health probes use the IP which doesn't match your cert SAN. Envoy is doing SNI-based routing and rejects the connection.

maria-support: Short-term fixes: 1) Set the health-check Host to "prod-service.internal" in the target group so the probe sends correct SNI; 2) OR change health check to TCP (no TLS) and have an internal health responder; 3) OR add a certificate that covers the node IP (not recommended).

lee-network: Also check any transparent TLS inspectors / egress proxies on the path — they can strip SNI or rewrite. But since this is intra-VPC IP target it should be direct; likely just the Host being blank.

customer.ops: Making change now: editing target group -> Health check -> Host = prod-service.internal. Applying...

deploy-bot: Target group health check update completed (by customer.ops) — 1852001340

customer.ops: After change, seeing targets 3/3 healthy within 30s and 502s cleared. Confirming metrics returning to baseline.

alice-oncall: Nice. I've added a note to the incident: root cause = health-check Host unset -> NLB used IP as SNI -> Envoy SNI mismatch -> handshake failure. Recommended remediations noted.

maria-support: Followups: can you add an explicit health check host during future rollouts to avoid this, and add a test step to your deploy playbook: "openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <host>" and also test with a raw connect to ensure no non-SNI path required.

jake-devops: Also recording this in runbook: if you use SNI-based routing in Envoy, always set health-check host or switch to TCP health checks for pure L4 probes.

customer.ops: Thanks all, will close once post-deploy runs clean for an hour. :thumbsup:

maria-support: Closing notes: customer fix confirmed, no further action required from infra. Marking as resolved in support ticket. :white_check_mark:
